title: A Mixtape for the Yearbook
premise: Vesper Nystrom has spent four years in the small town of Halvard keeping her head down, counting days to graduation, until history teacher Mr. Okafor pairs her with Delia Marsh—the girl whose family name is on the courthouse and whose brother led the harassment that made Vesper's life hell—for a semester project: an oral history of the town's shuttered mill. Digging through tapes and yearbooks, they uncover that Vesper's late grandmother and Delia's grandfather were once best friends who split over a decades-old injustice at the mill, a wrong that echoes into the present when the town council plans to demolish the site and bury the record. As the girls' uneasy alliance deepens into something neither will name, Vesper must choose between a safe scholarship exit and broadcasting the truth at the school's final spring audition—where she performs a mixtape of recovered voices, forcing Halvard to hear what it spent fifty years forgetting.
about_author: Kestrel Zhou grew up in a fading paper-mill town where the library kept more secrets than the courthouse did. They write stories about queer kids who refuse to be footnotes in other people's histories.

chapters.title: Ninety-Seven Days
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She maps her countdown to graduation on her bedroom ceiling and endures another day of slurs in the halls of Halvard Consolidated. When Mr. Okafor announces semester pairings, she gets Delia Marsh. Beat: dread sharpened into defiance.

chapters.title: Assigned Seating
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. First project meeting in the empty archive room; Delia arrives defensive, pre-loaded with apologies she won't say. They agree on the mill's oral history because neither wants to talk about anything real. Beat: cold truce.

chapters.title: The Tape Deck in the Attic
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Searching her grandmother Ruth's belongings for mill-era photos, Vesper finds a shoebox of cassette interviews labeled in two handwritings—Ruth's and someone named E. Marsh. Beat: grief interrupted by curiosity.

chapters.title: Delia's Version of Everything
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. At the Marsh house, Delia hides the project from her brother Cody, home on probation, and lies about where she goes after school. She recognizes Ruth Nystrom's name from her grandfather Earl's funeral stories. Beat: guilt as inheritance.

chapters.title: Rules of Engagement
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The girls negotiate terms: no personal questions, no mention of Cody, split the work. Vesper plays one tape; Earl's young voice describes a 1974 accident the official record calls 'operator error.' Beat: wary alliance with a crack of wonder.

chapters.title: Operator Error
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Library research shows the mill fatality report was sealed by petition—filed by Earl Marsh himself. Delia insists there's an explanation; Vesper says the explanation is always money. Beat: first real argument, first real honesty.

chapters.title: Cody at the Gas Station
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Cody corners Vesper outside work, all charm and threat, telling her to keep his sister out of trouble. Vesper records him on her phone without thinking. Beat: fear transmuted into evidence.

chapters.title: The Demolition Notice
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. The council posts plans to raze the mill by June 1—before graduation. Delia realizes their primary sources will literally be bulldozed, and that her family's name is on the demolition contract. Beat: stakes go public.

chapters.title: Side B
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A tape reveals Ruth and Earl were best friends who gathered worker testimony after the accident—until Earl recanted, took settlement money, and cut Ruth off. Vesper hears her grandmother's fury and, underneath it, love. Beat: inherited heartbreak.

chapters.title: Detention Economics
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Caught passing files, both girls get detention; Okafor quietly extends their archive access instead of punishing them. In the quiet hours Delia admits she's known about Cody for years and said nothing. Beat: confession as first intimacy.

chapters.title: What the Yearbook Didn't Print
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The 1975 yearbook shows Ruth and Earl together, then not. They track down Millie Okonkwo, a retired seamstress who was there the night of the accident—and who agrees to record new testimony. Beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Millie's Testimony
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Millie describes the unguarded machine, the foreman's order to keep working, and how the company bought silence one family at a time—including the Nystroms', which is why Ruth never spoke either. Beat: the past stops being abstract.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Late night in the archive, shoulder to shoulder over a shared earbud, Delia almost kisses Vesper and doesn't. She drives home shaking, past Cody's truck in the driveway. Beat: want versus loyalty.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Someone reports their project to the principal as 'disruptive'; Okafor is told to restrict them to textbook sources. Vesper suspects Cody got to someone. Beat: institutional pressure, rising paranoia.

chapters.title: The Scholarship Letter
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Her state arts acceptance arrives—full ride, due May 15, contingent on staying out of controversy. Her mother begs her to just finish quiet. Beat: the exit door opens exactly when staying matters most.

chapters.title: Cody Finds the Tapes
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Cody discovers the recordings and burns the duplicates in the Marsh fire pit, calling it family business. Delia films him doing it, then can't decide if she's brave or a traitor. Beat: betrayal inside the betrayal.

chapters.title: Two Truths, One Town
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The girls fight: Vesper accuses Delia of protecting her name again; Delia says Vesper's always had a bag packed. They don't speak for nine days while the mill demolition date nears. Beat: rupture at the lowest point.

chapters.title: Millie's Kitchen Table
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Millie convenes surviving mill families; half refuse, but enough sign sworn statements. Delia signs her own name to the petition to save the mill records, publicly breaking with her grandfather's legacy. Beat: choosing inheritance over legacy.

chapters.title: Audition Sign-Ups
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Spring showcase auditions open; performing means an audience, and an audience means the mixtape—Ruth's voice, Millie's voice, the truth—played over the PA to the whole school and the council members invited to 'celebrate' the demolition. Beat: decision crystallizing.

chapters.title: Sound Check
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The night before, Vesper and Delia rebuild the burned testimony from backups, Millie's re-recordings, and the phone video of Cody. Delia asks Vesper to play her voice on the tape too—a Marsh confessing. Beat: reconciliation as collaboration.

chapters.title: A Mixtape for the Yearbook
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. At the showcase, Vesper performs the mixtape live: voices of the mill, the sealed report read aloud, Cody's threat played clean. The gym goes silent, then Millie stands, then others. The council vote collapses; the demolition stalls. Beat: catharsis, justice outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ninety-seven days later than she planned to care, Vesper walks across the stage with Delia's hand briefly in hers. The mill becomes a memorial archive with both grandmothers' names on the plaque. Vesper leaves for the scholarship—not escaping, but carrying the town's true record with her. Beat: earned, unsentimental hope.
